issues.title: Exact key-bitmap mode for join Bloom filter on dense integer build keys
issues.hypothesis: Join BFs are hashed and approximate (sector-blocked BloomFilter in bloom_filter.hpp). Each probe pays a hash plus a lookup and still passes false positives through to the hash join. Dense integer FK keys (partkey, suppkey, orderkey, custkey) are common. When max-min of the build keys is at most about 128*build_count, one bit per key value gives an exact filter at similar memory, with no hashing and no false positives. A previous run on this workload measured -9.5..-12.4% on q09 (lineitem scan CPU 5.28→4.55s, rows exactly 3.27M), -10.5..-11.5% on q16, and -15% on q21 (l2/l3 scans 0.83/1.06s → 0.38/0.53s). The cap had to be 128 bits/key; at 64, the q21 delim BFs stayed hashed and the gain was only -4.9%. The current best (E0005) now builds BFs on the first key of multi-key HJs, so more joins benefit.
issues.plan: 1) BloomFilter (src/include/duckdb/planner/filter/bloom_filter.hpp, src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp): add an exact mode: SetExactRange(min, range) allocates ceil(range/64) uint64 words; InsertKeys/LookupKeys work on raw integer values (v - min), and values outside the range miss. 2) In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters / PushBloomFilter (src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp), decide exact mode from the raw final min/max. Gate: a single equality condition that is a BF candidate, NULLs not equal, left type == right type, 8..64-bit integer key, no storage_offset on the pushdown column (keep the existing rule that offset columns get no BF), and range < min(2^32, 128*ht.Count()). 3) Fill it: in JoinHashTable::Finalize (join_hashtable.cpp, next to InsertFirstKeyIntoBloomFilter), when the BF is in exact mode, read key column 0 from the row layout and set the bits instead of hashing. Bits must be set atomically, or per-thread with an OR, if the fill is parallel. 4) Probe: in BFTableFilter::Filter, take the exact path that skips HashInternal. Use UnifiedVectorFormat, and slice first if sel is set and the vector is not flat (SEQUENCE vectors). FilterValue handles exact mode too. In CheckStatistics, prune by range overlap, but never return ALWAYS_FALSE when NULLs pass. 5) Keep the hashed path unchanged for everything else. Verify correctness against SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown' on TEMP tables, including keys at min/max boundaries, negative keys, and INNER vs IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.
issues.expected_gain: q09 -10%, q16 -10%, q21 -10..-15% (prior measurements), and possibly q05/q07/q08 a few %. Geomean about -3..-4%.
issues.generality: Any hash join on a dense integer key (surrogate or FK keys, the dominant pattern in star/snowflake schemas) whose probe side is a scan that can take a pushed BF. Queries with sparse keys keep the hashed BF and are unaffected. A small slowdown is possible when the bitmap (up to 128 bits/key) exceeds cache where the hashed BF fit, but the cap keeps it at most the pointer table size.
issues.risk: Medium. Off-by-one errors at range boundaries, mishandled sel or SEQUENCE/constant vectors, or a statistics prune that returns ALWAYS_FALSE incorrectly would produce wrong results. The gate and tests above cover these.
